stem.text: Part of the structure of strobilurin is shown. $R$ and $R^{\prime}$ are inert groups.
Strobilurin is warmed with aqueous sulfuric acid producing compound X. Compound X is then treated with hydrogen in the presence of a nickel catalyst producing compound Y.
What could be the structure of compound Y?

A.alt: Skeletal formula option A: R-substituted chain with a methyl branch; the branched carbon bears a COOH group and a CH2–R' group.

B.alt: Skeletal formula option B: R-substituted chain with a methyl branch; the branched carbon bears a CH(OH)(OCH3) group and a CH2–R' group.

C.alt: Skeletal formula option C: R-substituted chain with a methyl branch; the branched carbon bears a CH2OH group and a CH2–R' group.

D.alt: Skeletal formula option D: R-substituted chain with two hydroxyl groups and a methyl branch; the chain carries a COOH group and a CH(OH)–R' end group.
